name: Erriscope – Site Incident Alerts for WooCommerce
author: TinySharp

sections.description:
Find the cause, not just the error.

Erriscope is a WordPress error monitoring and incident diagnostics plugin for site owners, developers, agencies, and WooCommerce stores.

Instead of leaving you with raw log lines, Erriscope groups repeated failures into clear incidents, identifies the likely plugin, theme, file, or request area when evidence is available, and tracks verification, recovery, and recurrence.

It works as a standalone WordPress monitoring plugin. When WooCommerce is active, Erriscope automatically adds checkout, cart, payment, and failed-order monitoring without changing orders, stock, gateways, checkout settings, or customer sessions.

Why use Erriscope?

  • Turn repeated PHP errors and fatal crashes into grouped incidents
  • See severity, occurrence count, lifecycle, and recovery status in one dashboard
  • Identify likely plugin, theme, WordPress Core, or file attribution when evidence is available
  • Monitor failures across frontend requests, REST API calls, admin AJAX, and WP-Cron execution paths
  • Compare incidents with recent plugin, theme, and PHP file changes for root-cause context
  • Receive grouped incident and recovery email digests instead of repeated alert noise
  • Use WooCommerce monitoring automatically when WooCommerce is installed
  • Run the Free plugin locally without an Erriscope account or license

WordPress error monitoring

Erriscope monitors runtime failures that occur while WordPress is executing requests and background work, including:

  • PHP warnings and user warnings
  • Fatal errors and critical runtime failures
  • Errors triggered during frontend, REST API, admin AJAX, and WP-Cron requests
  • Local loopback health-check failures
  • Incident recurrence after a previous recovery
  • Recent plugin, theme, and file changes that may help explain an incident

No monitoring plugin can report a runtime error before the affected code runs. Erriscope records the failure when WordPress executes the relevant request path.

WooCommerce checkout and payment monitoring

When WooCommerce is active, Erriscope adds read-only Store Health signals for revenue-sensitive failures, including:

  • Checkout exceptions and Store API server failures
  • Cart Store API failures
  • Repeated payment-failure patterns grouped by gateway
  • Failed-order patterns and recovery signals
  • Checkout and cart configuration health

Erriscope observes these signals without creating test orders, processing payments, changing gateway settings, modifying stock, or altering customer sessions. WooCommerce HPOS compatibility is declared, while WooCommerce remains optional.

Incident lifecycle and recovery tracking

Repeated occurrences with the same incident fingerprint stay grouped as one incident. Erriscope increases the occurrence count, verifies whether the signal is still failing, records recovery evidence, and can reopen the incident if the same problem returns.

This keeps the dashboard useful and prevents one recurring fault from creating hundreds of duplicate rows.

Smart incident email

Erriscope groups incident bursts into digest emails instead of sending one message for every repeated occurrence. A queued notification can be cancelled when the issue resolves before delivery, and recovery events can be grouped into a recovery digest.

Local email uses your existing WordPress wp_mail() transport, including an SMTP plugin when one is configured.

Safe deep fatal capture

Erriscope can install a managed wp-content/fatal-error-handler.php drop-in so it can preserve fatal-error context before WordPress Recovery Mode replaces it.

It never overwrites a fatal handler owned by another plugin or hosting provider. If another handler already exists, Erriscope reports the conflict and continues using the monitoring paths that remain available. Its own managed drop-in is removed when the plugin is deactivated or deleted.

Privacy by design

Erriscope Free performs its monitoring and stores incident data locally on your WordPress installation. It does not require an account, license, payment connection, or external monitoring service for local diagnostics.

The Free plugin does not send incident data to Erriscope servers. Local availability checks may request your own site URL and the local Erriscope health endpoint on the same WordPress installation.

Free core and optional Pro add-on

Erriscope Free is a complete local monitoring and diagnostics plugin. A separately distributed commercial add-on can extend it with independent 24/7 remote monitoring, server-side downtime alerts, advanced notification channels, deeper WooCommerce payment diagnostics, longer history, and private commercial updates. The commercial add-on is not included in this WordPress.org package.

Trademark Notice

WooCommerce and its associated marks are trademarks of Automattic Inc. Erriscope is an independent product and is not affiliated with or endorsed by Automattic.
sections.installation:
1. Install Erriscope – Site Incident Alerts for WooCommerce from WordPress.org, or upload the plugin folder to /wp-content/plugins/.
  2. Activate Erriscope.
  3. Open Erriscope in WordPress Admin.
  4. Review email recipients, recovery and warning email preferences, local health checks, and resolved-history retention.
  5. When WooCommerce is installed and active, Store Health monitoring is enabled automatically.
  6. If another fatal-error-handler.php drop-in already exists, review the conflict notice before relying on deep fatal capture.
sections.faq:
Does Erriscope work without WooCommerce?

Yes. Erriscope monitors WordPress and PHP failures, local health, incident lifecycle, recent changes, and recovery signals on standard WordPress sites. WooCommerce-specific monitoring appears only when WooCommerce is active.

Does the Free plugin require an external service?

No. Free monitoring, incident storage, diagnostics, and local email notifications run on your WordPress installation.

Is Erriscope a replacement for the PHP error log?

Erriscope complements the PHP error log. It turns supported runtime signals into grouped incidents with severity, occurrence counts, likely component attribution, recovery state, and diagnostic context. Server and PHP logs can still provide additional low-level evidence.

Will Erriscope detect an error in code that never runs?

No. Runtime monitoring can detect a failure only after the affected code executes. Erriscope covers relevant frontend, REST API, admin AJAX, WP-Cron, and WooCommerce request flows when they run.

What does WooCommerce monitoring observe?

It observes checkout exceptions, Store API server errors, cart API failures, repeated payment-failure patterns, failed-order patterns, and recovery signals. It does not modify orders, stock, gateways, checkout settings, carts, or customer sessions.

Why do repeated errors appear as one incident?

Occurrences with the same incident fingerprint are grouped so the dashboard and email remain useful. The occurrence count increases while Erriscope tracks verification, recovery, and recurrence.

What does Resolved history retention mean?

It controls how long resolved incidents remain in local history. Active and verifying incidents are not removed by retention. The allowed range is 7–365 days, and the default is 30 days.

Can I clear incident history manually?

Yes. Clear all incidents removes active, verifying, and resolved incident history together with pending digest state. Detection remains enabled immediately afterward.

What happens when I deactivate or delete the plugin?

Deactivation preserves settings and incident history while removing the managed fatal-capture drop-in and scheduled hooks. By default, deletion also preserves persistent incident data. Enable Delete stored data on uninstall before deletion when you want Erriscope to remove its incident tables and settings permanently.

Where can I get support?

Use the Erriscope support forum on WordPress.org. Include your WordPress version, PHP version, whether WooCommerce is active, and a redacted description of the incident. Never post passwords, API keys, license keys, customer data, or private server credentials.

What is Erriscope Pro?

Erriscope Pro is a separate commercial add-on for remote monitoring and additional commercial capabilities. It is not required for the local monitoring and diagnostics provided by Erriscope Free.
sections.changelog:
1.0.0

  • Initial stable Free release.
  • Detects PHP warnings, fatal errors, and critical runtime failures with plugin, theme, or file attribution when evidence is available.
  • Covers frontend, REST API, admin AJAX, and WP-Cron execution paths.
  • Adds incident grouping, occurrence counting, verification, automatic recovery, recurrence tracking, and manual incident-history clearing.
  • Adds grouped incident and recovery email digests without repeated messages for the same unchanged incident.
  • Adds local WordPress loopback health monitoring and runtime schedule self-healing.
  • Adds WooCommerce checkout, Store API cart, payment-failure pattern, failed-order, and recovery monitoring.
  • Declares WooCommerce HPOS compatibility while keeping WooCommerce optional.
  • Adds managed deep-fatal capture without overwriting a fatal handler owned by another plugin or host.
  • Keeps the complete WordPress.org Free core separate from the optional commercial add-on.
